headline: Meta's Muse AI agent app has come to the iPad, with new connections to work apps such as Asana, Canva, Figma and QuickBooks.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by 2: the iPad launch was announced on 7 Oct 2026, nine days before the window, and the new facts are an install estimate and a recap of known complaints.
importance_line: People who link their email, shopping and work accounts to Muse hand an AI agent more of their digital life, and sites such as Amazon can block it, but the install figure is an estimate and the update itself is a week old.
summary: Mashable reports that Meta's Muse, a free app in which an AI agent books, orders and buys for users once they connect their accounts, is now available on iPad, as announced in a 7 Oct 2026 Threads post, and that its App Store notes list connectors for Asana, Canva, Dropbox, Figma, QuickBooks, GitHub, Klaviyo, Zoom, Granola, Notion and Meta ad accounts. The iPad version and the connectors date from earlier this month; new in this report are an estimate of 6.6 million installs, Mashable's note that Amazon has taken steps to block Muse, and a recap of complaints that Muse shared a user's home address and read private messages without permission.
notes: Read Mashable in full. Continues the 12 Oct pool item on Muse gaining ad-account access and business tools; the iPad announcement itself is dated 7 Oct 2026 and Muse's mobile debut 8 Sep 2026. The complaints are as reported by Mashable (one user's address; columnist Jason Aten's allegation).
